issues.description: Method name mismatch for the static delivery method on SealSaloon: the problem statement UML and the template Main expect a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) on SealSaloon, but the solution's SealSaloon class defines a static method named receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity). Because the template Main calls acceptSupplyDelivery(...), the different name in the solution means the expected method is missing, which will cause compilation errors and confuses students about which method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's SealSaloon.receiveDelivery(...) method to acceptSupplyDelivery(...) with the signature public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity), or add a static acceptSupplyDelivery wrapper that delegates to receiveDelivery. Also update any template/example calls or the problem statement to use the same method name so students and tests reference the same identifier.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named 'acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int)' on SealSaloon to handle supply deliveries into the shared Stock. The solution implementation instead declares a static method named 'receiveDelivery(String, int, int)' in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java. Both methods represent the same concept (accepting a supply delivery and updating/adding a StockIngredient), but they use different identifiers. This mismatch prevents a clear mapping from the requirement ('acceptSupplyDelivery') to the provided implementation ('receiveDelivery') and can cause confusion or test failures for students who implement or use the API as documented.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Rename the solution method 'receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)' to 'acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)' (keeping it static and preserving the signature and behavior), or alternatively update the problem statement and tests to require 'receiveDelivery' instead of 'acceptSupplyDelivery'.
